cv-99cfaed4.stem: Which statement about the small saphenous vein is correct?
options: It runs under the deep fascia, inside muscle.
It passes in front of the medial malleolus.
It drains into the femoral vein.
It passes behind the lateral malleolus and usually drains into the popliteal vein.
It runs with the saphenous nerve.
cv-99cfaed4.explanation: The small saphenous vein begins at the lateral edge of the foot, rises behind the lateral malleolus to the midline of the calf and opens into the popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa. In the calf it runs with the sural nerve.

cv-efdf82fd.stem: At which level is the inferior vena cava formed, and at which level does it pass through the diaphragm?
options: Formed at L5, passes through the diaphragm at T8.
Formed at L1, passes through the diaphragm at T10.
Formed at S1, passes through the diaphragm at T10.
Formed at L4, passes through the diaphragm at T12.
Formed at L3, passes through the diaphragm at T8.
cv-efdf82fd.explanation: The two common iliac veins unite at L5, to the right of and slightly below the aortic bifurcation, to form the IVC. The IVC passes through the caval opening in the central tendon of the diaphragm (T8).

cv-147eede0.stem: Which vein opens into the superior vena cava from its right posterior side?
options: Hemiazygos vein
Right subclavian vein
Internal thoracic vein
External jugular vein
Azygos vein
cv-147eede0.explanation: The azygos vein arches over the root of the right lung at T4 to open into the SVC. It collects the posterior intercostal veins and the oesophageal and bronchial veins; it is an important collateral route when the IVC is blocked.

cv-799fea3d.stem: Where, and by the union of which veins, is the hepatic portal vein formed?
options: At the porta hepatis, by the union of the right and left hepatic veins
At the lesser curvature of the stomach, by the union of the right and left gastric veins
Behind the neck of the pancreas, by the union of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins
In front of the duodenum, by the union of the left gastric and splenic veins
Behind the tail of the pancreas, by the union of the renal and splenic veins
cv-799fea3d.explanation: The portal vein forms at L1–L2 behind the neck of the pancreas; the inferior mesenteric vein usually opens into the splenic vein. The vein rises in the hepatoduodenal ligament, behind the bile duct and the hepatic artery.

cv-0cf94980.stem: A patient with alcoholic cirrhosis is brought in with massive haematemesis; examination shows dilated veins around the umbilicus (caput medusae) and haemorrhoids. Which portocaval anastomosis is the source of the bleeding?
options: Anastomosis between the left colic and renal veins
Anastomosis between the superior and middle rectal veins
Anastomosis between the paraumbilical and superficial epigastric veins
Anastomosis between the left gastric vein and the oesophageal veins (azygos system)
Anastomosis between the splenic and left renal veins
cv-0cf94980.explanation: In portal hypertension blood passes into systemic veins through collaterals: oesophageal varices at the lower oesophagus (their bleeding can be fatal), rectal varices in the anorectal region, caput medusae around the umbilicus and retroperitoneal anastomoses.

cv-0f81ede0.stem: In the neck, what is the position of the internal jugular vein relative to the common carotid artery?
options: Outside the carotid sheath, on the surface of the SCM
Medial to the artery, close to the trachea
Within the carotid sheath, lateral to the artery
Behind the artery, under the prevertebral fascia
In front of the artery, within the thyroid gland
cv-0f81ede0.explanation: In the carotid sheath the common carotid artery is medial, the internal jugular vein lateral and the vagus nerve behind both. When a central line is placed, the vein is sought in the triangle between the two heads of the SCM, lateral to the artery.

cv-90f888e4.stem: When the jugular venous pressure (JVP) is observed, which vein visible in the neck crosses the SCM superficially?
options: Facial vein
Vertebral vein
Middle thyroid vein
External jugular vein
Internal jugular vein
cv-90f888e4.explanation: The external jugular vein descends obliquely over the surface of the SCM and opens into the subclavian vein above the clavicle. It becomes distended in right heart failure. The JVP itself, however, is properly assessed on the internal jugular vein.

cv-8f6a9c14.stem: What is the most common serious complication of subclavian vein catheterisation, and why?
options: Haemopericardium, because the vein opens directly into the pericardium
There is no air embolism, because the vein has valves.
Phrenic nerve palsy, because the nerve passes through the vein
Pneumothorax, because the cervical pleura (cupula) lies just behind and below the vein
Chylothorax, because the thoracic duct is on the right side
cv-8f6a9c14.explanation: The subclavian vein runs between the clavicle and the 1st rib, in front of the anterior scalene. The pleura and the apex of the lung lie just behind it, so a needle advanced too deeply causes a pneumothorax. Because the thoracic duct drains into the left venous angle, left-sided procedures carry a risk of chylothorax.

cv-f04b527e.stem: Which superficial vein in front of the elbow is used most often for taking blood?
options: Axillary vein
Cephalic vein
Median cubital vein
Brachial vein
Basilic vein
cv-f04b527e.explanation: The median cubital vein links the cephalic to the basilic vein and lies on the bicipital aponeurosis, which protects the brachial artery and median nerve beneath it.

cv-09c0276c.stem: Where does the cephalic vein open into a deep vein?
options: Into the brachial vein at the elbow
Into the basilic vein in the axilla
Into the brachial vein at mid-arm
Into the axillary vein, after passing through the deltopectoral groove
Into the external jugular vein in the neck
cv-09c0276c.explanation: The cephalic vein rises on the lateral side of the forearm and arm and, through the groove between deltoid and pectoralis major, pierces the clavipectoral fascia to open into the axillary vein. The basilic vein, by contrast, pierces the deep fascia at mid-arm and joins the brachial veins to form the axillary vein.

cv-9d3e524c.stem: Which option gives the correct drainage route of venous blood inside the skull?
options: Inferior sagittal sinus → cavernous sinus → external jugular vein
Transverse sinus → superior sagittal sinus → vertebral vein
Cavernous sinus → straight sinus → external jugular vein
Sigmoid sinus → transverse sinus → confluence of sinuses → internal jugular vein
Superior sagittal sinus → confluence of sinuses → transverse sinus → sigmoid sinus → internal jugular vein
cv-9d3e524c.explanation: The dural sinuses collect blood from the brain, meninges and skull. The superior sagittal sinus also contains the granulations through which CSF is absorbed. The sigmoid sinus continues as the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen.

cv-b1671c8b.stem: Where does the left testicular vein drain, and what is the clinical importance of this?
options: It drains into the internal iliac vein and so causes haemorrhoids.
It drains into the inferior vena cava, so varicocele is not seen on the left.
It drains into the azygos vein and so causes chest pain.
It drains into the portal vein and so dilates in portal hypertension.
It drains into the left renal vein, so varicocele is more common on the left.
cv-b1671c8b.explanation: The right testicular vein opens obliquely into the IVC, while the left testicular vein enters the left renal vein at a right angle. The left renal vein can also be compressed between the aorta and the SMA (nutcracker). That is why dilatation of the pampiniform plexus (varicocele) is mostly left-sided.

cv-51ef5367.stem: Which statement about the left renal vein is false?
options: It passes between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta.
Its compression between the aorta and the SMA causes 'nutcracker' syndrome.
It receives the left gonadal and left suprarenal veins.
It passes behind the aorta to open into the inferior vena cava.
It is longer than the right renal vein.
cv-51ef5367.explanation: The left renal vein normally passes in front of the aorta, just below the SMA. A retroaortic left renal vein is a rare variant. Because the left renal vein is long, the left kidney is usually preferred for transplantation.

cv-25ce6332.stem: Which route plays the main role in the spread of infections from the 'danger triangle' of the face to the cavernous sinus?
options: Superficial temporal vein → superior sagittal sinus
Pterygoid plexus → maxillary vein → external jugular vein
Retromandibular vein → external jugular vein
Facial vein → internal jugular vein → sigmoid sinus
Facial vein → angular vein → superior ophthalmic vein
cv-25ce6332.explanation: At the medial angle of the eye, the angular vein – the beginning of the facial vein – communicates with the valveless superior ophthalmic vein. Infections around the nose and upper lip can reach the cavernous sinus by this route and cause thrombophlebitis.

cv-98cd4a4d.stem: Which statement about the left brachiocephalic vein is correct?
options: It is longer than the right and passes obliquely in front of the branches of the aortic arch.
It is shorter than the right and descends vertically.
It opens directly into the right atrium.
It passes behind the aorta.
It receives the azygos vein.
cv-98cd4a4d.explanation: On each side the internal jugular and subclavian veins unite behind the sternoclavicular joint to form the brachiocephalic veins. The left brachiocephalic vein crosses to the right behind the manubrium and joins the right one to form the SVC. The thoracic duct opens into the left venous angle.
